findings.title: Eight production seams still do wall-clock datetime arithmetic across DST; the forecast grid lands 60 min off
findings.claim: On every 2025-2027 Europe/Stockholm transition day the real coordinator cycle executes datetime arithmetic at 9 distinct production sites whose result differs from the UTC truth (8 instances plus tariff._window_slot, a wall-clock label by definition), and the worst (_forecast_arrays' step_offset) puts step 0 of the price/weather grid 60 min away from the solve anchor on 42 of 48 cycles.
findings.mechanism: Home Assistant hands every datetime the process-wide ZoneInfo instance; CPython subtracts two aware datetimes that share one tzinfo object as naive wall clock, and datetime+timedelta on a zoned value is wall-clock addition. _forecast_arrays computes step_offset=(now-midnight) in wall minutes, then _utc_step_starts walks UTC from midnight by that many steps, so after the transition the grid is 1 h late (spring) or early (autumn) and the plan is priced against the wrong hour for ~21 h. tests/dst_checks.py freezes only 00:07 (offset 0) so it never runs this path.

findings.title: Python closures miss every file a spawned child process reads; select() skips the script on a change to it
findings.claim: 31 (script, file) pairs across tests/doc_claims.py and tests/deployment_shape.py, and 883 across entities.py, features.py and harness_headers.py, are files the script's child processes read that the script's committed closure omits, so closure.select([file]) returns mode scoped with the script skipped; a one-line tests/hastub edit turns deployment_shape.py red while select() skips it.
findings.mechanism: tests/closure.py:_exec_record records a Python script in-process under sys.addaudithook plus sys.modules. A child process's reads never reach the hook, and only the child's argv is kept. The node lane records under strace -f, but the Python lanes do not. tests/closure.py check re-records with the same blind instrument, so the table is checked against itself and cannot flag these seams. findings.title: Mutation ratchet inventory cannot see 528 of 2313 production guard seams; a new guard of those shapes raises it by 0
findings.claim: tests/mutation_table.py:candidates() yields no site on 528 of the 2313 guard seams in custom_components/heatpump_optimizer (52 of 1346 early-exit ifs, 246 of 668 clamps, 230 of 299 threshold ternaries). A new undispositioned guard whose test spans two lines therefore raises unpinned_sites by 0 and ratchet_refusal does not refuse, against +1 and refusal for the same guard on one line.
findings.mechanism: Six single-line operators. GUARD_OFF fires only on an if whose test is on one line, whose line starts with 'if ' and ends with ':', and which has no else; that misses multi-line tests (46), elif (3), a trailing comment after the colon (2) and else branches (1). CLAMP_DROP fires only on a bare min/max with exactly 2 args on one line; that misses numpy/math clamps (179), multi-line calls (63) and 3+ args (4). No operator touches a conditional expression's test. At their pre-fix commits, two of the six ledger I1 instances whose defect is a guard line are of an invisible shape: R5 D3-04 #1312 (the ternary len(positives) >= 2, 076f4a35^) and R5 D3-08 #1316 (np.clip in curve_learning._step_down, 6438f8f6^).

findings.title: Expert setup: the zones page says 'leave defaults if you don't need two-zone' and leaving them turns two-zone on
findings.claim: Walking the initial flow's 'Enter thermal values directly' path and submitting every page as pre-filled creates an entry that ThermalParameters.from_config reads as two_zone_enabled=True (1), while the describe path at the same defaults reads False (0).
findings.mechanism: async_step_zones declares the zone fields vol.Optional(..., default=DEFAULT_...), so the frontend posts them and voluptuous refills them even when cleared; the step stores them with self._data.update(user_input). ThermalParameters.from_config's 'auto' two_zone_mode infers two-zone from the presence of any of those keys, and the initial flow never writes two_zone_mode. quick_setup.derive guards the same fact explicitly (writes two_zone_mode on/off, its comment: adding zone keys 'is what silently flips a house to 2-zone'); the zones page, its sibling seam, does not. The page description promises the opposite. The overview then says 'House: two zones' for a single-zone house; the only way back is the options flow's two_zone_mode, which the page never mentions.
